text: `portal spawn <sessions…>` mirrors the picker's commit exactly: it reuses its calling terminal window as one of the N (self-attach last via AttachConnector or SwitchConnector, in or out of tmux) and spawns the N−1 others, through the same pre-flight, sequential spawn, per-window ack and self-attach-last flow.

text: `portal spawn --detect` is a dry-run that only prints the detected terminal identity (friendly name and bundle id) and opens nothing; `portal spawn` with no session arguments and no `--detect` is a usage error.
why: Detection must be callable without spawning.

text: On success `portal spawn` self-execs away into the tmux attach and never returns, so there is no success exit code.
why: The CLI has no TUI; its reporting maps to stderr and exit status, which tests assert on.

text: `portal spawn` exits 1 with the picker's one-line message on stderr, and self-execs nothing, on a pre-flight abort, a partial spawn failure, or an unsupported/NULL terminal with N≥2; on permission-required it exits 1 with the permission guidance (target terminal and Automation-settings hint) on stderr.
why: The picker's in-band banners map to stderr and exit status.

text: A `portal spawn` usage error (no sessions and no `--detect`, or an unknown flag) exits 2.
why: The CLI's reporting is stderr and exit status.

text: The picker always self-attaches to exactly one of the N, reusing its own window: outside tmux by exec'ing `tmux attach` (AttachConnector), which replaces the picker process; inside tmux by `switch-client` (SwitchConnector).
why: The no-leftover-window rule forces the picker to own its own window reuse.

text: Each spawned window runs the existing `portal attach <session>` command, from a fresh shell outside tmux; `portal spawn` is not what runs in the spawned windows, nor does the picker re-run `portal open` there.
why: The selection is already made, and `portal attach` is the existing Portal-mediated attach chokepoint, using the same connector the picker uses.

Running bare `tmux attach` in the new windows.

text: `portal attach <name>` already existed (`cmd/attach.go`): it validated the session and called the same connector the picker used, switch-client inside tmux and exec of `tmux attach-session -t =<name>` outside; resume and hydration ran eagerly at bootstrap, not at attach, so a bare `tmux attach` would not have skipped resume hooks, and the reason to use `portal attach` is consistency through one chokepoint.
how: Read against the code during research (review-002 F1).

text: Order is load-bearing: detect the host terminal; spawn the N−1 windows, one adapter call per window, collecting each window's ack; only after all N−1 confirm, exec self into the Nth session.
why: The self-exec is a point of no return, so the spawns must complete first; one call per window isolates failures.

text: The N−1 windows spawn running `<os.Executable()> attach <session>`, the picker's own absolute binary, not a bare `portal` PATH lookup; as a side effect `portal` need not be on PATH.
why: The warm-command latch is version-gated; a PATH-resolved portal of another version would read it unsatisfied and full-bootstrap per window, while the picker's own binary guarantees parity.

text: Ghostty's `command` execs an argv, not a shell, in a bare PATH (`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` plus Ghostty's bin), with no Homebrew or login PATH, so `tmux` and anything portal shells to would not be found.
how: Validated live on Ghostty during discussion.

text: The picker builds the spawned command as an env-self-sufficient argv: `/usr/bin/env PATH=<picker's full PATH>` ahead of `<os.Executable()> attach <session> --spawn-ack <batch>:<token>`, a real argv, never shell syntax.
why: So tmux and anything portal shells to resolve whatever bare environment the host terminal provides.
rules_out: Each adapter injecting PATH through a per-terminal env property (such as Ghostty's environment variables property).

text: Only a minimal, explicit env is injected, never a snapshot of the picker's whole environment: PATH is the only required variable, and any future addition is named explicitly.
why: Inject the minimal set, not a blanket copy.

text: TMUX and TMUX_PANE must not be propagated into the spawned command; a picker triggered from inside tmux explicitly strips them.
why: The spawned N−1 are fresh host windows that must run out of tmux, so their `portal attach` takes the exec-attach path, not switch-client.

text: Env delivery is one uniform mechanism for native adapters and config recipes: the composed command carries its own env, so no adapter needs a per-terminal env property and no terminals.json recipe needs an env slot; adapters and recipes run `{command}` verbatim.
why: Recipe authors only describe opening a window running a command, never PATH plumbing.

text: What triggers multi-select, and how does it coexist with the Sessions keymap?
Lowercase `m` enters an explicit multi-select mode from the normal Sessions list, a real mode you can sit in with zero selected; uppercase `M` stays retired.

text: In the mode, `m` again toggles the cursor row in or out of the selection: the same key enters the mode and toggles marks.
why: No second key and no reuse of an already-meaningful one.
rules_out: `x`, which already means Sessions/Projects.
`Tab`.
Repurposing `Space`, which must stay preview.

text: Enter is commit in both modes: normal mode attaches the cursor row, multi-select mode opens the marked set through the pre-flight and spawn flow.
why: Enter stays commit.

text: Esc exits multi-select mode and clears the selection.
why: The mode's cancel.

text: Grouping HeaderItem rows are non-selectable and skipped by marking and navigation (the existing skipHeaderRow invariant).
why: Existing invariant.

text: N=1 (one marked, Enter) spawns nothing and degenerates to a plain single attach in the current window, with no special-casing; N=0 (nothing marked, Enter) is a no-op that exits multi-select mode back to the standard picker, as Esc does.

text: In the mode `Space` (preview), `/` (filter) and `s` (regroup) stay live.
why: Preview is a firm user requirement, still useful while selecting; filter and regroup help find things to mark.

text: In the mode `k` (kill), `x` (page-toggle), `r` (rename) and other row actions are suppressed.
why: Row actions don't apply to a selection.

text: While the `/` filter is focused, `s` and `m` are literal filter characters: the filter input owns typing.
why: The focused input owns its keys.

text: Selection is sticky across filtering, paging, regrouping and the Space-preview round-trip; on return from preview `rebuildSessionList` re-renders in-mode with the selection intact, pruning only a session externally killed during the preview; a row filtered out stays selected and reappears when the filter clears.
why: Consistent with the pre-flight rule: a gone session can't be opened.

text: Filter is an inner sub-state of multi-select: while the filter is focused it owns Enter and Esc (commit-to-browse, clear-filter), and multi-select's Enter (open marked) and Esc (exit mode) apply only when it is not focused.
why: The filter already owns those keys whenever focused, so there is no new conflict.

text: The single notice-band header slot time-shares by focus: filter focused shows the orange filter line and filter footer, otherwise the multi-select banner and footer; one claimant at a time, and selections persist underneath while filtering.
why: Single-slot arbiter.

text: Multi-select is as unmistakably a distinct mode as filtering: its own mode colour and a banner in the notice-band slot, which it owns while in mode, reading e.g. `N selected · m toggle · space preview · ⏎ open · esc cancel`.
why: Modelled on filter mode.

text: Selected rows carry a glyph marker and the mode colour, never colour alone.
why: Modern Vivid's NO_COLOR / colourless-render rule.

text: The Paper design fixes the mode's glyph and copy: a `●` marker on selected rows, and the footer `↑↓ navigate · m toggle · ␣ preview · ⏎ open · esc cancel`.
why: The delivered Paper frames, approved by the user, fix the exact glyph and copy.

why: One slot, highest wins.

text: On an unsupported terminal, entering multi-select shows the multi-select banner (the unsupported banner steps aside), and the unsupported warning re-asserts at the N≥2 Enter block.
why: Follows the notice-band precedence.

text: This feature ships per-session marking only.
why: Group-select is deferred.

text: Selection is a set of session identities, not list rows: in By Tag mode a multi-tag session renders as several rows, and toggling any one marks the session, so `●` shows on all its rows and the `N selected` count counts distinct sessions; a mark survives regroup, filter and paging.

text: What is the contract when a burst does not fully complete, because a spawn or attach fails or the user aborts?
The contract concerns genuine spawn/attach partial failure, not bootstrap contention, which the warm-command latch dissolves.
why: Each attach takes the abridged fast-path.

text: On Enter, before opening any window, pre-flight verifies every selected session still exists (quick has-session checks); if any is gone the batch aborts atomically: nothing spawns, no window opens, no self-attach, and a one-line error names the gone session(s) (`⚠ '<session>' is gone — nothing opened`).
why: The dominant failure is a session killed between picker-load and Enter, and catching it before any window opens makes failing completely clean.
rules_out: Best-effort-with-report: open what you can, report failures, then attach, which dragged in a report surface, an r retry and a deferred self-attach.
alternatives: Best-effort-with-report.

text: A pre-flight abort prunes the gone session(s) from the selection and keeps the surviving marks, staying in multi-select mode, so a second Enter proceeds with the survivors rather than re-aborting.
why: The same prune-what's-gone rule as the preview round-trip.

text: After pre-flight the N−1 spawn sequentially and their acks are collected; when all confirm, the trigger window self-attaches silently, with no success nag.
why: Self-attach last, gated on all N−1 confirming.

cites.section: Decision — pre-flight + all-or-nothing; self-attach gated on all-succeeding

text: When a spawn fails after pre-flight passed, Portal does not close or undo the windows that opened: it leaves them in place, skips the trigger window's self-attach so the user stays in the picker, and shows a one-line error naming the window that failed.
why: Portal doesn't own those host windows and won't rely on untested terminal teardown for a rare hiccup.
rules_out: Rolling back by closing the windows that opened.

cites.section: Refinement (specification phase, 2026-07-11) — post-pre-flight failure: leave-what-opened, not rollback

text: On a post-pre-flight failure Portal unmarks the sessions whose windows opened and keeps the failed or un-acked ones marked, so a second Enter retries exactly the missing set.
why: The trade-off accepted for a model with no report surface and no teardown.

text: `osascript` returning success only confirms the terminal accepted the request, not that the window rendered, portal ran, the session existed or the attach happened.
how: Reasoned in discussion and restated in the spec.

cites.section: Decision — confirmation mechanism: token ack (not tmux-watching)

text: Confirmation is an explicit token ack: the picker issues a batch id and a per-window opaque token, threads them into each spawned command as `--spawn-ack <batch>:<token>`, the spawned `portal attach` writes its `@portal-spawn-<batch>-<token>` marker right before exec, and the picker watches for the markers with a timeout; a missing marker at timeout is a failed spawn.
why: A direct signal from Portal's own spawned process, immune to how many other clients are attached, so a session already attached elsewhere confirms correctly.
rules_out: tmux client-watching (diffing list-clients), fragile while lingering mosh clients churn the client list during the burst.

cites.section: Decision — confirmation mechanism: token ack (not tmux-watching)

text: The ack channel is a namespaced `@portal-spawn-<batch>-<token>` tmux server option behind a small ack seam (write-token / collect-tokens), where batch and token are picker-generated option-name-safe ids (nanoid-style), never the renameable session name.
why: A session name can hold characters invalid in a tmux option name, which would make set-option fail and read as a false timeout; server options die with the server.

cites.section: Decision — confirmation mechanism: token ack (not tmux-watching)

text: The only all-server-options enumerator, `ListSkeletonMarkers`, skipped any name not prefixed `@portal-skeleton-` (`internal/state/markers.go`), so a distinct `@portal-spawn-` prefix is invisible to it and namespacing isolates sweeps both ways.

text: The server-option channel is deliberately daemon-readable: the deferred remember-and-restore-workspace follow-on can teach the 1s-tick daemon to read the same markers as an additive change; forward-compatibility only, not built here.
why: No rewrite of how the picker collects acks later.

text: The ack timeout is per window, not global: each window's timer starts when its spawn fires.
why: Under sequential spawn a single clock from Enter would over-report late windows as failed.

cites.section: Decision — confirmation mechanism: token ack (not tmux-watching)

text: A named `spawnAckTimeout` constant, default about 8 s per window; its expiry classifies that window a failed spawn, and it is tunable.
why: Generous headroom over the measured ~260 ms osascript open plus the window's abridged attach.

text: Does the ~8 s spawnAckTimeout hold against real abridged-attach timing? The spec leaves it to be confirmed at build.

The ack fires at the last instant before exec, since portal is replaced once it execs into tmux; it confirms the window opened, portal ran, the session was found and the attach handoff is starting, and the final handoff is essentially guaranteed from there.
how: Reasoned in discussion and restated in the spec.

text: The picker cleans its batch markers before self-exec and on a pre-flight abort or a reported spawn failure; leaks from a late ack or a crashed picker are bounded, expire with the server and never collide; a defensive `@portal-spawn-*` sweep mirroring CleanStaleMarkers is deferred, a drop-in if ever needed.
why: Unique batch ids and server-lifetime options make leaks harmless.

text: The ack is carried by a `--spawn-ack <batch>:<token>` flag added to the existing `portal attach`, part of the composed argv, which puts attach in spawn-ack mode and names the marker to write, with no derivation from the session name.
why: It flows through `{command}` and recipes uniformly with no env slot.

text: In spawn-ack mode attach runs the abridged bootstrap, confirms the session exists, writes `@portal-spawn-<batch>-<token>` (value opaque, presence the signal), then execs into tmux; the write is the last action before the handoff.
why: The honest boundary the ack depends on.

text: The marker write is best-effort: attach still execs if it fails, and the picker times out and classifies that window failed; a session that fails to resolve at attach writes no marker, with the same result.
why: A failed write is safe: it reads as a failure.

text: The picker runs the burst as an async tea.Cmd streaming progress and per-window ack results back as tea.Msgs, as the cold-path concurrent bootstrap does, never blocking the Update loop.

text: While spawning and awaiting acks the picker shows a pending affordance in the notice band, e.g. `Opening n/N…`.

why: Prevents races between user input and the completion handler's selection change, so the retry-only-what's-missing guarantee rests on a well-defined selection.

text: Ctrl-C/Esc mid-burst returns to the picker in multi-select mode (it does not quit Portal), aborts the remaining spawns, leaves already-opened windows in place, cleans the batch markers, unmarks the sessions whose windows opened and keeps the rest marked; after the self-exec there is nothing to cancel.
why: Self-exec being last keeps cancellation clean, and selection follows the partial-failure rule.

text: The N−1 spawn sequentially, one adapter call completing before the next fires; reversible, flipped to parallel only if a future validation shows it safe and meaningfully faster (parallel spawn is deferred).

text: How does the feature behave across trigger contexts: in or out of tmux, a selected session attached elsewhere or gone, and a selection including the current session?

text: A clean NULL and a transient detection error (a ps or defaults read failure) both resolve to the unsupported no-op path; a transient error also emits a spawn-component WARN.
why: A breadcrumb tells the two apart.

text: An N≥2 Enter landing before detection resolves awaits it, then proceeds by its result (supported spawns, NULL or error is the unsupported no-op); an in-flight identity is never treated as unsupported merely for being unresolved.
why: The gate distinguishes in-flight from a resolved NULL.

text: The unsupported/unconfigured banner, naming the detected identity, surfaces proactively over the normal list on Sessions-page entry; it is an info banner, not a modal.
why: The user knows the terminal is unsupported before marking anything; a modal hides everything.

text: Multi-select stays available on an unsupported terminal, and Enter with N=1 proceeds regardless of detection as a plain self-attach needing no adapter.
why: Multi-select may serve future non-spawn actions, and single attach needs no adapter.

text: Enter with N≥2 on an unsupported or NULL terminal is an atomic no-op, nothing opens, and the unsupported banner is re-asserted naming the detected identity.
why: Only external-window spawning needs the adapter; the asymmetry with N=1 is intentional.

text: What shape is the adapter contract, and how does it extend across terminals and future capabilities?

macOS-first and Ghostty only to begin with; no Windows; Linux is not a goal, loosely supported and never tested, with a Linux user able to configure their own command, so the design degrades to bring-your-own-command and no Linux adapters are written.
why: The user's terminal is Ghostty on a Mac; AppleScript being Mac-only is fine.

text: Both built-in Go adapters (Ghostty ships in this feature) and the user-config layer (terminals.json) ship in this feature, as two implementations of one contract; new built-in terminals land by open-source PR.
why: The user may override the native Ghostty command (e.g. add a resize) and will test that path; users of other terminals and the long tail need it.

text: Detection resolves identity, a resolver maps identity to an adapter, and the adapter only opens windows; detection is not an adapter method.
why: Detection is separate from the adapter.

cites.section: Decision — generic contract (B), detection separate, capability-based
Detection is separate from the adapter

text: Resolution precedence is config override, then native adapter, then unsupported; config can override a built-in too (e.g. Ghostty plus a resize), and a NULL or unmatched identity is unsupported.
why: Config wins so an override is always possible; the conventional config-over-default layering.

text: The adapter's single job is to open a new host window running a given command, `OpenWindow(command)`, not attach to a session; the spawn layer composes the command (`<os.Executable()> attach <session>` plus the ack token) and hands it over.
why: Keeps adapters dumb and portable, keeps the attach-and-ack composition in one place, and lets the same primitive run other commands later.
rules_out: A session-aware `OpenAttached(session)`, which would bake portal attach into every adapter and scatter the composition.
alternatives: (A) session-aware OpenAttached(session).

cites.section: Decision — generic contract (B), detection separate, capability-based
Generic contract: open a window running a command

text: Each adapter owns its terminal-specific concerns: how it opens a window running the command, and quarantining all OS/terminal specifics behind a typed result; env and PATH are not an adapter concern.
why: The composed command is env-self-sufficient.

text: Adapters implement exactly one capability in scope, open-window-with-command; future introspect and place-on-space slot in as additive optional capabilities (Go interface segregation, checked by type assertion) without touching existing adapters, the mechanics an implementation concern.
why: So v1 doesn't paint the architecture into a corner for the workspace-restore and Spaces follow-ons.

cites.section: Forward-Looking (out of scope — "keep half an eye")
Decision — generic contract (B), detection separate, capability-based

text: Where does the user config live, what shape is it, and how does a complex command such as a multi-line AppleScript live in it?
The config is `~/.config/portal/terminals.json`, following Portal's JSON-store convention and XDG-resolved through the existing configFilePath; user-authored and read-only at spawn time.
why: Matches projects.json and hooks.json.

text: Each entry maps an identity matcher key (friendly alias, .app name, raw bundle id or `*`-glob) to `commands` → `open` (the only capability key in scope) → a recipe; future introspect or place are additive sub-keys, not a breaking change.
why: Config and adapter extend in lockstep.

text: A recipe is either `argv`, an inline argv-array template (not a string, to avoid shell quoting, and named argv to avoid colliding with the placeholder), or `script`, a path to a file Portal runs.
why: Explicit fields are clearer than probing the disk.
rules_out: Auto-detecting whether a value is a path on disk to treat it as a script.

text: The placeholder is `{command}`, substituted with `<os.Executable()> attach <session>` plus the ack token; config expresses only how a terminal opens a window running `{command}`, not `{session}`.
why: Follows the generic open-window contract.

cites.section: Generic contract: open a window running a command

text: `{command}` substitutes as a single already-resolved, env-prefixed command string dropped literally into the recipe; escaping it for an embedding context such as an AppleScript string is the recipe author's responsibility.
why: The author wrote that AppleScript; the argv form exists so CLI terminals avoid quoting.

text: A `script` recipe receives `{command}` as `$1`; Portal expands a leading `~` in the path and executes the file directly (it needs its exec bit and shebang), and a missing or non-executable script is an invalid entry, skipped with a WARN.
why: The standard contract for an executable escape-hatch script.

text: A config recipe's non-zero exit maps to spawn-failed, otherwise the ack decides the window's fate; permission-required is native-adapter-only, so recipes never trigger the burst-stopping permission path.
why: Portal cannot read AppleEvent codes from a generic argv or script.

text: A malformed or unreadable terminals.json is ignored whole, resolution falling through to native adapters then unsupported, with a spawn-component WARN.
why: Malformed input must degrade safely, never crash the picker, consistent with Portal's tolerant stores.

text: An entry's recipe must carry exactly one of argv or script, and its template must contain `{command}`; otherwise the entry is skipped (falling through to native, then unsupported) with a WARN naming the key; unknown capability sub-keys are ignored for forward-compatibility.
why: A window with no `{command}` would never run the attach; every rejection leaves a breadcrumb so a typo is diagnosable.

text: Within config the most specific entry wins: exact raw bundle id, then exact .app name or friendly alias, then `*`-glob, a longer glob beating a broader one and a bare `*` lowest.
why: A user's specific override always beats their glob fallback.

text: How are the first-run macOS Automation (TCC) permission and AppleEvent errors handled?

All terminal/OS specifics (AppleScript, osascript, the -1712/-1743 codes, TCC, macOS deep-links) live inside the terminal driver alone, which returns a typed result: permission-required (with guidance), unsupported, or spawn-failed; general code switches on the category and never sees an AppleScript string or AppleEvent number.
why: Every future driver gets the same clean contract and each new terminal stays cheap.

cites.section: Decision — driver-quarantined error handling + blocking-modal flow

text: With Ghostty's AppleEvents grant reset (`tccutil reset`), a fresh spawn succeeded with no dialog and no TCC row recreated: Ghostty scripting Ghostty through osascript is self-exempt, and since Portal always spawns the terminal it runs in, the path is always self to self; Portal is never the TCC subject, the host terminal is.
how: Tested live during discussion.

TCC is self-exempt — no first-run gate (validated live)

text: There is no TCC first-run prompt or gate in the normal flow.
why: The AppleScript path is always self to self, so always exempt.

why: Catches an unexpected denial rather than doing nothing.

text: Within a burst a permission-required result counts as a failed window (skip self-attach, leave opened windows, keep the affected session marked) and stops the burst, surfacing the permission guidance once for the batch rather than the generic spawn error.
why: Spawns are sequential and the grant is per pair, so every later window would hit the same wall; a retry after granting proceeds.

What persistent state and daemon machinery does the feature touch, and how is it observed?

Near-zero persistent state: the feature reads terminals.json, writes only transient `@portal-spawn-*` tmux server options (self-cleaned, not files, not captured), and does not touch sessions.json, the daemon capture loop, prefs.json or the restore machinery.
why: Traced in discussion; the daemon's capture is structural, not a server-option dump.

text: The spawn flow gets its own `spawn` log component, a deliberate amendment to Portal's closed logging taxonomy, with a closed event catalog emitted from the spawn chokepoint: detection outcome, adapter resolution, per-window spawn and ack outcome, permission-required, and batch summary.
why: Spawn observability without call-site inventions.

text: Spawn logs one INFO cycle summary (e.g. `spawn: opened 11/14`) and DEBUG per window, and the driver's OS-specific detail rides as an opaque `detail` attr.
why: Matches bootstrap/restore/daemon instrumentation and keeps the vocabulary closed under the driver quarantine.

text: The spawn component's closed attr keys are `batch`, `terminal`, `bundle_id`, `resolution` (config | native | unsupported), `session`, `ack` (confirmed | timeout | failed), `opened` / `total`, and `detail`; `total` is N including the trigger's target, and `opened` counts each acked spawn plus the trigger's self-attach when it happens.
why: Spec-governed keys, as bootstrap/restore/daemon enumerate theirs.

text: Resume hooks registered in hooks.json vanish silently after a tmux server kill/restart or reboot: Portal reopens with "No sessions available" in the project picker, the hooks never fire, and no error or warning is shown. Reproducible always, with two or more panes each carrying an on-resume hook.
how: Observed by the person on a real server restart and reported from the inbox bug report; the reproduction steps are recorded in the log.

text: The bug affects any local system using tmux and Portal with several panes holding registered resume hooks. It was first observed on 2026-04-01 on a freshly installed MacBook Pro, the first real test of the feature on new hardware; there is no workaround, and it has likely always been this way, never having been tested against a server restart.
how: Recorded from the person's report in the log's environment notes.

text: Severity is high: every user relying on resume hooks for session continuity is affected, and the core workflow of restoring Claude Code sessions after a restart is broken.
how: Assessed in the log's impact notes.

text: Both attach and open call the hook executor, which runs hooks.ExecuteHooks; ExecuteHooks (internal/hooks/executor.go:66-68) calls tmux.ListAllPanes() and then store.CleanStale(livePanes) unconditionally, and CleanStale (internal/hooks/store.go:130-159) keeps only hooks whose pane ID is in the live set and removes the rest from disk.
how: Traced through the code: cmd/attach.go, cmd/open.go, cmd/hook_executor.go, internal/hooks/executor.go, internal/hooks/store.go.

text: ListAllPanes() (internal/tmux/tmux.go:235-241) runs tmux list-panes -a -F #{pane_id} and on error (no server, no sessions) returns an empty slice and a nil error, so its caller cannot tell "no panes" from "tmux not ready", and ExecuteHooks's err == nil check always passes.
how: Read in internal/tmux/tmux.go during the code trace.

text: The clean command (cmd/clean.go:77-80) already skips cleanup when the live pane list is empty and hooks exist; that guard was added during the resume-sessions-after-reboot work but was never replicated in ExecuteHooks.
how: Read in cmd/clean.go during the code trace.

text: Root cause, problem 1 (data loss): after a server restart ListAllPanes() returns an empty slice with no error, CleanStale() reads that as no panes existing, and every hook entry is deleted from hooks.json before it can fire. CleanStale is a pure filter with no awareness of whether an empty live set is meaningful, and the cleanup is best-effort with errors ignored, yet a wrong cleanup loses data rather than merely missing a cleanup.
how: Concluded from the code trace.

text: A synthesis agent independently confirmed the root cause of problem 1 with high confidence and no gaps.
how: Recorded in the log's notes from the investigation's synthesis pass.

text: Root cause, problem 2 (broken mapping): hooks are registered keyed by $TMUX_PANE (cmd/hooks.go:83-98), and tmux pane IDs (%0, %1) are ephemeral, reset when the server restarts, so even hooks that survive deletion either fire in the wrong context when a new pane reuses the ID or never fire. The volatile server-option markers are just as volatile as the pane IDs.
how: Read in cmd/hooks.go and the hook store during the investigation.

text: The original design assumed tmux pane IDs persist across tmux-resurrect, as its research and specification both stated; they do not: resurrect assigns new pane IDs. This false assumption is the root cause of problem 2.
how: Found by examining tmux-resurrect's restore approach against the original research and specification.

text: Session names are non-durable ({project}-{nanoid}, session/naming.go:41), so they cannot be matched by name alone across restarts, though the project prefix is stable; the session name is however passed to ExecuteHooks and can scope the lookup.
how: Read in session/naming.go and the executor during the investigation.

text: tmux-resurrect's save and restore scripts target panes by session_name:window_index.pane_index for send-keys and select-pane during restore, so session names, window indices and pane indices survive a resurrect while pane IDs (%N) are reassigned by the server on restart.
how: Confirmed by examining tmux-resurrect's save/restore scripts.

text: The bug went uncaught because the test "no tmux server running skips cleanup gracefully" (executor_test.go:537-568) asserts that CleanStale is called with an empty live list, validating the buggy behaviour; CleanStale is mocked there, so no data is removed; no integration test covers the server-restart scenario end to end; and the feature was built and tested on a machine whose tmux server was always running.
how: Read in internal/hooks/executor_test.go and the feature's history.

text: Directly affected: internal/hooks/executor.go (cleanup path and hook matching), internal/hooks/store.go (data model keyed by pane ID), cmd/hooks.go (registration by $TMUX_PANE) and all resume hook functionality. Potentially affected: cmd/clean.go, which calls CleanStale on the same pane-ID model, and internal/hooks/executor_test.go, whose test validates the buggy behaviour.
how: Assessed from the code trace.

text: How should the fix make resume hooks survive a tmux server restart and fire again when Portal reopens sessions?
The fix addresses both problems, hook deletion and pane ID instability: the feature must work end to end, not just have its data loss fixed.
why: The person identified that the inbox bug report also flagged pane ID instability; fixing the deletion alone would leave hooks unable to find their panes after a restart.
rules_out: Option A, the empty-pane guard alone: it prevents data loss but hooks still cannot find their target panes after restart because pane IDs change

text: ExecuteHooks skips CleanStale when len(livePanes) == 0, matching the existing guard in cmd/clean.go:77-80.
why: Prevents hook data loss on server restart, when ListAllPanes returns an empty slice.

text: What durable key should hooks be stored and matched by, in place of the ephemeral pane ID?

Hooks are keyed by tmux's structural address, session_name:window_index.pane_index (the tmux session name, the zero-based window index within the session and the zero-based pane index within the window; a colon between session and window, a dot between window and pane), replacing pane IDs.
why: Session names, window indices and pane indices survive tmux-resurrect, which uses the same addressing internally for send-keys targeting during restore; the key uniquely identifies each pane, handles several panes per session and fails gracefully without resurrect.
rules_out: Keying by pane ID: pane IDs do not survive a restart or resurrect
Option B, keying by project path: durable but cannot tell several panes in one project apart, so a project with three Claude sessions would hold one hook entry, not three
alternatives: Option A — empty-pane guard only
Option B — key by project path
Option C — key by structural position (chosen)

text: hooks.json maps structural_key → map[event]command (e.g. {"my-project-abc123:0.0": {"on-resume": "claude --resume abc"}}) in place of pane_id → map[event]command; the store's map key changes from pane ID to structural key.
why: The storage model follows the new key.

text: Hook registration (hooks set in cmd/hooks.go) no longer keys by $TMUX_PANE: a new tmux.Client method resolves the current pane's structural key from $TMUX_PANE (e.g. tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" "#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}"), and the hook is stored under that key.
why: The pane ID is only the way to find the current pane; the durable key is its structural address.

text: When ExecuteHooks(sessionName) runs, it queries the session's panes with their window and pane indices and looks hooks up by sessionName:windowIndex.paneIndex.
why: Matching by structural key finds each pane's hook after a resurrect restores the same structure.

text: ListPanes(sessionName) and ListAllPanes() change their tmux -F format string from #{pane_id} to #{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}, returning structural keys; their signatures stay []string, only the meaning of the strings changing.
why: Callers receive the key the store is keyed by with no signature churn.

text: SendKeys(target, command) uses structural keys directly as tmux -t targets (e.g. tmux send-keys -t "my-project-abc:0.1" "command" Enter), with no resolution back to pane IDs.
why: tmux natively accepts session:window.pane as a target, the same approach tmux-resurrect uses.

text: The PaneLister, AllPaneLister and KeySender interface signatures stay []string / string, their values changing from pane IDs to structural keys; no new interfaces are added, and test mocks change to structural key values.
why: The change is in the values, not the shapes.

text: Volatile markers are named @portal-active-{structural_key} (e.g. @portal-active-my-project-abc:0.0) in place of @portal-active-%paneID, and MarkerName takes a structural key.
why: Markers follow the hook key; tmux user options accept colons and dots in names.

text: CleanStale keeps its signature as CleanStale(liveKeys []string), the parameter renamed: callers pass structural keys from ListAllPanes and it cross-references hook map keys against them, its semantics unchanged but for the key format.
why: Stale cleanup judges hooks by the same key they are stored under.

text: hooks rm resolves the current pane's structural key instead of using $TMUX_PANE, and removes the hook entry and the volatile marker by that key.
why: Removal must find the entry registration wrote.

text: The Hook struct's PaneID field becomes a structural key field, List() fills it with structural keys, and hooks list displays structural keys instead of pane IDs.
why: The listing shows the key hooks are now stored under.

text: portal clean (cmd/clean.go) moves to the structural key model for cleanup, keeping its existing empty-pane guard.
why: It calls CleanStale on the same model as ExecuteHooks.

text: How should hooks behave where tmux-resurrect is absent, with several panes per session, and when execution finds nothing to match?

Without tmux-resurrect the server restarts with no sessions: hooks stay on disk, the empty-pane guard preventing their deletion, but nothing matches them, so they do not fire, with no errors and no data loss.
why: The person required graceful failure without resurrect; this is correct best-effort behaviour.

text: Portal does not check for, detect or explicitly depend on tmux-resurrect; resurrect is the expected setup, and the structural key approach works with it naturally.
why: The person's priority: Portal has no awareness of resurrect by design.

text: Each pane in a session has its own hook entry keyed by its structural position: a session with three panes has three independent entries (e.g. proj-abc:0.0, proj-abc:0.1, proj-abc:0.2).
why: The person required multiple panes per session, each with its own hook.

text: Hook execution failures (no matching panes, stale keys) are silent: no error is surfaced to the user.
why: Matches the existing best-effort design.

text: What happens to existing pane-ID-keyed hooks.json entries, and how should the change ship?

The hooks.json format change is a breaking change with no explicit migration: old pane-ID-keyed entries (e.g. %0) match no live structural key and are removed by CleanStale on its first run with live panes after the upgrade.
why: Acceptable since the current format produces broken behaviour anyway.

text: Ship the fix as a regular release.
why: A breaking change to the hooks.json format is fine, since the current format produces broken behaviour.

text: Fix complexity is medium: the keying change touches registration, execution, storage, cleanup and the CLI surface, though each change is mechanical. Regression risk is medium: existing hooks become invalid under the new hooks.json format.
how: Assessed in the log's risk assessment.

text: What tests should the fix carry?
Fix the test "no tmux server running skips cleanup gracefully" (executor_test.go:537-568) to assert CleanStale is not called when livePanes is empty.
why: It currently validates the buggy behaviour.

text: Add a test for hook survival when ListAllPanes returns empty (the post-restart, pre-resurrect case).
why: Covers problem 1's data loss directly.

text: Add tests for structural key construction, registration and lookup.
why: Covers the new keying model.

text: Add tests for hooks on multiple panes in the same session using structural keys.
why: Covers the multi-pane requirement.

text: Add a test verifying a graceful no-op when structural keys match no live pane (the no-resurrect case).
why: Covers graceful failure without resurrect.

text: Update every existing hook test to use structural keys instead of pane IDs.
why: The values the interfaces carry change from pane IDs to structural keys.

text: After `tmux kill-server`, opening Portal with `x` outside tmux shows the 'starting tmux server' loading page, then lands on the projects page: no sessions are restored and resume hooks never fire, with no error output from Portal. Afterwards no tmux server is running at all. Reproduced on a separate MacBook Pro (macOS, Ghostty), not the dev machine.
how: The person's reproduction: two Claude Code sessions with registered resume hooks, `tmux kill-server`, then `x` from a fresh Ghostty terminal, then `tmux list-sessions` from another terminal.

text: The affected machine has tmux-resurrect and tmux-continuum installed with `@continuum-restore 'on'` and `@resurrect-capture-pane-contents 'on'`, and its tmux.conf does not set `exit-empty off`; the hypothesis that resurrect was missing is ruled out.
how: Confirmed on the affected machine during the investigation.

text: Impact assessed as high severity: every user relying on resume hooks after a server restart loses their Claude sessions on a tmux restart, a core workflow disruption.
how: The investigation's impact assessment.

text: Root cause: Portal's `EnsureServer()` (`internal/tmux/tmux.go:137-145`), called from `PersistentPreRunE` in `cmd/root.go`, calls `StartServer()` (`tmux.go:125-131`), which runs `tmux start-server`. That starts a server and sources `.tmux.conf` but creates no sessions; once the `start-server` client disconnects, tmux's default `exit-empty on` makes the server loop see zero sessions and exit, before tmux-continuum can restore anything.
how: Code trace of Portal's bootstrap, checked against tmux's source (`server.c`, `cmd-kill-server.c`, `server-client.c`) and its man page entry for `start-server` (tmux issues #182 and #936); a synthesis agent validated the root cause and independently verified every Portal code path.

cites.section: Bug: Server Exits Before Session Restoration

text: tmux-continuum's restore is asynchronous and delayed: on detecting a fresh server (its `#{start_time}` check) it backgrounds `continuum_restore.sh`, which sleeps 1 second before calling resurrect's `restore.sh`. The server dies from `exit-empty` in that gap, so the restore then fails silently against a dead server.
how: Read from tmux-continuum's source (`continuum.tmux`, `continuum_restore.sh`).

cites.section: Bug: Server Exits Before Session Restoration

text: `ListSessions()` (`internal/tmux/tmux.go:79-83`) swallows errors and returns `[]Session{}, nil` when the server is dead, so Portal can't tell 'no sessions yet' from 'server is dead'.
how: Read from Portal's code during the trace.

cites.section: Bug: Server Exits Before Session Restoration

text: With no destination, `open` launches the TUI on its loading page (`serverStarted=true`), which fetches sessions, re-polls every 500 ms while the list is empty, and after the 6 s max wait calls `transitionFromLoading()` → `evaluateDefaultPage()`, which lands on the projects page when there are no sessions: so against the dead server it silently polls for 6 s and lands on projects.
how: Read from `cmd/open.go` and `internal/tui/model.go` during the trace.

cites.section: Bug: Server Exits Before Session Restoration

text: tmux-continuum's own systemd/launchd bootstrap uses `tmux new-session -d`, not `tmux start-server`, so the server has a session keeping it alive through the delayed restore; and resurrect's `restore.sh` has a 'restoring from scratch' mode that, on detecting exactly 1 pane, replaces the bootstrap session with the saved state and cleans up the default session "0" if it wasn't in the save file.
how: Read from tmux-continuum's `continuum.tmux` and tmux-resurrect's `restore.sh`.

text: Portal chose `start-server` deliberately: the original auto-start-tmux-server discussion rejected a bootstrap session to avoid lifecycle complexity, acknowledging that tmux exits with no sessions by default and assuming continuum would create sessions before that happened, with a keepalive session to be added later if not. That assumption was wrong, since continuum's restore is async with a 1-second delay; the deferred edge case has now materialised.

text: How should Portal bootstrap the tmux server so it stays alive until continuum restores the saved sessions?

Replace `tmux start-server` with `tmux new-session -d` in `StartServer()`, creating a detached bootstrap session that keeps the server alive through plugin initialisation and continuum's delayed restore; resurrect's restoring-from-scratch mode replaces that session with the saved state.
why: It follows tmux-continuum's own proven bootstrap pattern rather than inventing a new mechanism, and addresses the root cause directly.
evidence: tmux-continuum's systemd/launchd bootstrap uses `tmux new-session -d`.
Resurrect replaces a single-pane bootstrap session with the saved state.

text: The bootstrap session is created with bare `tmux new-session -d` and no explicit session name, so tmux names it "0".
why: Resurrect's restoring-from-scratch logic cleans up session "0" when it wasn't in the save file; a custom name would not be recognised by that cleanup.
rules_out: A custom bootstrap session name.

text: What may the fix change?
The fix is scoped to `StartServer()` in `internal/tmux/tmux.go` alone: no changes to hooks, the TUI, its polling, or any other component.

text: How should Portal behave after the fix in each server and resurrect state?

Server killed, resurrect installed with a save: the bootstrap session is created, continuum restores the saved sessions, resurrect replaces the bootstrap session, Portal shows the restored sessions and hooks fire.
why: The bootstrap session keeps the server alive through continuum's delayed restore.

text: Server killed, resurrect installed but no save: bootstrap session "0" persists and Portal shows the sessions page with one session.
why: With nothing to restore, resurrect replaces nothing.

text: Server killed, resurrect not installed: bootstrap session "0" persists harmlessly and Portal shows the sessions page with one session.
why: The person wanted the fix to degrade gracefully without resurrect.

text: Server already running: no change; `EnsureServer()` returns `(false, nil)` and `StartServer()` is not called.
why: The bootstrap path runs only when no server is running.

text: CLI with a path argument, server killed: the bootstrap session keeps the server alive, `bootstrapWait()`'s polls find the restored sessions and the command proceeds normally.
why: The CLI bootstrap wait polled a dead server for the same reason as the TUI; a live server fixes both.

`EnsureServer()`'s return values stay unchanged: `(false, nil)` when the server was already running, `(true, nil)` when it was just started (now with a bootstrap session), `(true, err)` when a start was attempted and failed.

text: Degenerate key at registration: `portal hook set --on-resume` exits 0, prints nothing and persists an entry even when `$TMUX_PANE` names a pane that does not exist; the key collapses to the literal `:.` (empty session component, empty window and pane indices). Reproduced 2026-08-16 against Portal 0.11.0 with `TMUX_PANE=%165 portal hook set --on-resume 'noop'` on a dead pane, which added `":.": { "on-resume": "noop" }` to `hooks.json`; the entry was removable with `portal hook rm --on-resume --pane-key ':.'`, so the rm path accepts the degenerate key too. Reproducible always, given an unresolvable `$TMUX_PANE`.
how: Reproduced by hand against the installed Portal 0.11.0 on 2026-08-16, with a `%<n>` pane id that is not live.

text: Key drift over the pane's lifetime: the hook key bakes `window.pane` coordinates at registration and nothing re-keys the entry when the pane moves. tmux derives `pane_index` from layout position, so closing a sibling pane, closing a window under `renumber-windows on`, `break-pane` and `move-pane` change the coordinates; the key stops addressing its own pane and the daemon's stale sweep removes it, correctly by its own rule. Reproduced in an isolated `-L` socket: one unchanged pane went `t:1.2` -> `t:2.1` -> `t:1.1` across a break-pane and a window kill, three keys for one pane, and the sweep reaped the entry at the original key. Reproducible always, given any pane rearrangement.
how: Reproduced in an isolated tmux `-L` socket.

text: How the loss shows: no error at registration (exit 0, no output, entry present); nothing at production INFO names what was removed, the only trace of a prune being `hooks: clean-stale op=clean-stale entries=1`; `portal doctor` reports every check green, including `stale hooks: no stale hooks`; scrollback still restores, so a hookless pane looks healthy until the reboot that needed the resume; and it is detectable only by diffing `hooks.json` keys against the live pane list. Both failure modes end with a pane coming back from a reboot to a bare shell.

text: Restore renumbers windows and orphans the key it just fired: capture stores the pane's real `#{window_index}`, but restore recreates each extra window with `NewWindow('<session>:', …)`, passing no index, so tmux assigns the next free one. Wherever saved indices are non-contiguous they differ: the hook fires correctly on the first reboot (`collectArmInfos` bakes the key from saved state), then once `@portal-restoring` clears the sweep finds nothing answering to the saved key and reaps it, so the second reboot has no hook. This matches the standing note that reboot hooks do fire and hooks go missing between reboots. It is latent on the user's install, whose `renumber-windows on` keeps indices contiguous; it is general on tmux's default. The pane half is unaffected: `pane_index` is always contiguous and restore recreates panes in saved order.

text: `hooks.json` has no cross-process locking: no `sync.`, `Mutex`, `flock` or `Lock()` in `internal/hooks` or `internal/fileutil`. `Store.Set`, `Store.Remove` and `Store.CleanStale` each Load -> mutate -> `fileutil.AtomicWrite`; the write is atomic but the read-modify-write is not, and the writers are separate processes (the CLI against the daemon's 10 s sweep, and CLI against CLI). A sweep that loaded before a `hook set` writes its snapshot minus stale and loses the new key; the end state is indistinguishable from drift, with the intervening `clean-stale entries=1` naming a different key even at DEBUG.

The two named instances' four-minute gaps rule a race out for them; it is not ruled out for any other instance. Durable identity does not close it.

text: Root cause: the hook key is not a durable, verified reference to a pane. It is half identity and half position, and Portal never checks that a key it writes identifies anything. One defect surfaces at three moments: at write time (tmux exits 0 with `:.` and no layer validates), over the pane's lifetime (rearrangement changes the key and the sweep removes it), and at the reboot boundary (restore renumbers windows, so the hook survives exactly one reboot). `hooks.json` is written once and never revisited, so any value tmux may recompute rots when it changes; the session component was fixed by `@portal-id` and the pane component was left positional.
how: Concluded from the code trace and sandbox findings.

text: How does registration verify that `$TMUX_PANE` names a live pane?

text: How should a session's resume hook survive a rename of the session while its pane process keeps running?

Anchor resume hooks to an immutable, rename-immune Portal session identity, a tmux session user-option stamped at creation and carried on the session object rather than its name, mirroring the existing `@portal-dir` pattern, and key hooks off it instead of the mutable session name.
why: It is the only direction closing both trigger paths at the root, since nothing has to intercept the rename; it needs no change to the external SessionStart hook and reuses a proven pattern. Portal's own in-TUI rename triggering the same bug is what eliminated intercept-and-rekey as the primary fix.
rules_out: Intercept-and-rekey on rename, rewriting hooks.json keys old to new: only the in-TUI rename is interceptable, a tmux `session-renamed` hook is fragile and may not expose the old name, so external renames stay broken; it patches the symptom and leaves identity mutable.

Dropping per-pane structural addressing and keying purely by session id: breaks multi-pane support, since hooks are per-pane, and collapses into the stable-identity option once pane addressing is re-added.
alternatives: Intercept-and-rekey on rename
Key purely by session id

text: The identity is a new session user-option `@portal-id`, held in one shared constant `PortalIDOption = "@portal-id"` (as `session.PortalIDOption`, parallel to `session.PortalDirOption`), referenced by every set-option site (creation and the restore re-stamp) and kept in sync with the literal embedded in `tmux.HookKeyFormat`; its package placement is an implementation detail, so long as the stamp and re-stamp sites can import it.
why: One constant keeps every stamp site and the key format in agreement.

text: `@portal-id`'s value is a freshly generated opaque random token, a `crypto/rand` nanoid independent of the session name, frozen at creation, its width chosen so birthday collision across the whole session population is negligible (the existing `NewNanoIDGenerator` scheme, widened if warranted, an implementation detail).
why: An opaque token keeps the identity distinct from the name and can never collide with a session name.

text: The token is generated fire-and-forget, with no uniqueness check against existing `@portal-id` values; correctness rests on width alone, and the accepted residual of a duplicate id is hook-key cross-talk between the panes sharing it.
why: Width makes collision negligible, and fire-and-forget lets QuickStart stamp inside its argv chain, which has no Go-side collision-retry seam.

text: Once stamped, `@portal-id` is never rewritten: a rename, external or in-TUI, changes `#{session_name}` but leaves `@portal-id` untouched, so the hook key derived from it is stable across any number of renames.
why: Immutability is what makes the key rename-immune.

text: `SessionCreator.CreateFromDir` (`internal/session/create.go`) stamps `@portal-id` with a best-effort `SetSessionOption(name, PortalIDOption, <token>)` immediately after `NewSession`, beside the `@portal-dir` stamp, the token generated just before through the creator's injected id generator (`sc.gen`, the one used for names). A generation error or a `SetSessionOption` error is swallowed with no log component, leaving the session un-stamped on the name fallback; a stamp failure never aborts creation.
why: Mirrors `@portal-dir`'s stamping exactly and keeps stamping best-effort.

text: `QuickStart.Run` (`internal/session/quickstart.go`) adds a `; set-option -t <name> @portal-id <token>` step to its chained detached-create, stamp, attach `ExecArgs`, beside the `@portal-dir` step and before `attach-session` blocks the chain. The token is generated in Go inside `Run` through the injected id generator before `ExecArgs` is assembled and interpolated as a literal; a generation failure omits the step, leaving the session created and un-stamped.
why: The argv chain has no error seam, so the token must be ready before the chain is built; stamping stays best-effort.

text: The hook key becomes `<@portal-id or session_name>:window.pane`: a stamped session keys by its immutable id, and an un-stamped one (legacy, created by hand in tmux, or a stamp that failed) falls back to the session name, which equals the key already on disk. Un-stamped sessions never panic and degrade to the name-based key everywhere.
why: Existing hooks.json entries keep matching with no migration, the same un-stamped fallback role `@portal-dir`'s lazy resolver plays; the log had left the format's load-bearing nature and legacy sessions as constraints for the spec.

text: No backfill of `@portal-id` onto pre-existing sessions and no hooks.json re-key migration: the fix protects sessions created after it ships, legacy sessions keep working through the name fallback, and renaming one still orphans its hook until it is next recreated from scratch, when it gains an id and becomes rename-immune. After an upgrade an un-stamped, never-renamed session's entry still resolves and fires.
why: Legacy sessions migrate naturally as they are recreated, and the name fallback keeps their on-disk keys valid.

text: Every site that produces or consumes a hook key derives it by the identical rule, prefer `@portal-id` else `session_name`, suffixed `:window.pane`: the three producing sites (registration, stale cleanup, restore) and the consuming site (hydrate) must all agree.
why: Any site disagreeing orphans hooks, the bug itself.

text: `tmux.PaneTarget` stays exactly as it is, the canonical name-based `-t` target formatter for addressing live panes (`respawn-pane`, `select-pane`); the hook key becomes a separate concern with its own formatter, so the change touches only hook identity, not tmux targeting.
why: Keeps targeting and hook identity decoupled.

text: A new `internal/tmux` primitive `HookKeyFormat`, the tmux format string `#{?@portal-id,#{@portal-id},#{session_name}}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}` for live reads, which tmux resolves per session to `<id>:w.p` when stamped and `<name>:w.p` when not.
why: One shared live-read primitive keeps every live site on the same rule.

text: A new `internal/tmux` primitive `HookKey(portalID, name string, window, pane int) string`, a pure formatter for saved state returning `<portalID>:w.p` when `portalID` is non-empty, else `<name>:w.p`: the in-Go mirror of the tmux conditional.
why: Saved-state sites need the same rule without a live tmux read.

text: Retire the four stale doc-comments asserting a name-based formatter is the canonical hooks.json key: `PaneTarget` (`tmux.go:551-558`), `PaneTargetExact` (`tmux.go:572-573`), `StructuralKeyFormat` (`tmux.go:771-779`) and `ListAllPanes` (`tmux.go:781-798`, with its `ResolveStructuralKey` reference). The 'format is stable across releases, changing it silently invalidates every hooks.json entry' invariant transfers to `HookKey` and `HookKeyFormat`; the old primitives stay valid for name-based targeting and non-hook structural use but stop claiming hooks.json ownership.
why: Leaving any of them would invite a future caller back into name-based keying, re-establishing the drift the fix removes.

text: Registration: `resolveCurrentPaneKey()` in `cmd/hooks.go` resolves the hook key through a new client read using `HookKeyFormat` (e.g. `ResolveHookKey(paneID)`, `display-message -p -t <pane> <HookKeyFormat>`) instead of `ResolveStructuralKey`, so `portal hooks set` and `rm` store and remove under the stable key; `rm`'s `--pane-key` literal pass-through is unchanged.
why: Registration must store under the key the later stages derive.

text: `ResolveHookKey` is a single `display-message` read with the stamped-or-not choice made inside tmux, so there is no Go-side 'id absent' branch; a failed read aborts registration with the error, as `ResolveStructuralKey` does today, and never synthesizes a name-based key.
why: A synthesized name-based key would silently orphan a stamped session's hook.

text: Stale cleanup: the live-key enumeration feeding `CleanStale(liveKeys)` in `cmd/run_hook_stale_cleanup.go` and `cmd/clean.go` switches from `ListAllPanes()` / `StructuralKeyFormat` to live panes' hook keys through `HookKeyFormat`; the name-based `StructuralKeyFormat` and `ListAllPanes` stay for non-hook structural use. Cleanup thus never deletes a freshly restored hook and never mass-orphans existing hooks on upgrade.
why: This is the load-bearing consistency point: live keys produced by another rule than registration's would mass-orphan every stamped session's hook.

text: Restore: `collectArmInfos` in `internal/restore/session.go` sets `hookKey: tmux.HookKey(sess.PortalID, sess.Name, w.Index, p.Index)`, preferring the saved `@portal-id` from sessions.json, else the saved name, so the baked `--hook-key` matches what registration stored; base-index drift preservation is unchanged (saved indices for the key, live indices for the FIFOs).
why: Restore must bake the key registration stored under.

text: Hydrate (`cmd/state_hydrate.go`) is unchanged: it looks up `hooks.LookupOnResume(store, cfg.HookKey)` by the baked `--hook-key` and execs `sh -c '<hook>; exec $SHELL'` on a hit or bare `$SHELL` on a miss, which now hits for any renamed but stamped session. After restore re-stamps the live session, a later cleanup read of it yields the same key restore baked, so cleanup never treats a freshly restored hook as stale.
why: Stages 1 and 3 now agree on the stable key, so the consumer needs no change.

text: Portal persists `@portal-id` across reboots through sessions.json, unlike `@portal-dir`, which lazily re-derives and is deliberately not persisted: an opaque token can't be re-derived, and after a rename the id is unrecoverable unless saved.
why: tmux user-options are in-memory server state and don't survive a reboot; the headline case, renamed then rebooted, needs restore to recover the id to bake the matching key.

text: `state.Session` (`internal/state/schema.go`) gains one field, `PortalID string` with JSON key `portal_id`: additive and optional, an old sessions.json decoding to `""` and falling back to the name, an older binary ignoring it; no schema `Version` bump and no sessions.json migration.
why: A tolerant additive field keeps old and new binaries compatible both ways.

text: Capture (`internal/state/capture.go`) appends a session-scoped `#{@portal-id}` as the last column of `captureFormat`, bumping `captureFieldCount` from 10 to 11 in lockstep with the parser, so existing field indices are unchanged; an un-stamped session captures `PortalID == ""`. The alphanumeric token can't contain the `|||` delimiter.
why: `captureFormat` is fixed-arity and length-validated, so a field added without the count bump rejects or mis-slots every row; trailing placement moves the fewest reads.

text: The new column parses into a `portalID` field on `paneRow`, and `Session.PortalID` is lifted from the first row of `grouped[name]` returned by `parsePaneRows`, every pane row of a session carrying the same value. A session in `keep` with no pane rows (killed between enumeration and the pane read) yields an empty id and no windows, needing no guard, since `Restore` already rejects a session with no windows or panes.
why: The value is session-scoped, so any row carries it, and the zero-row case is never consumed.

text: Restore's `createSkeleton` (`internal/restore/session.go`) re-stamps the saved id immediately after `NewSessionWithCommand(sess.Name, …)`, best-effort, when `sess.PortalID` is non-empty (`_ = r.Client.SetSessionOption(sess.Name, PortalIDOption, sess.PortalID)`); a legacy session with no saved id stays un-stamped on the name key. The hook then keeps firing on every later reboot.
why: sessions.json is a snapshot regenerated from live tmux state, so without the re-stamp the id serves only the first resume: the next capture would erase it, post-restore cleanup would key the session by name and delete the hook that just fired, and a later rename would no longer be stable.

text: Hook firing never reads the live `@portal-id`: restore's order is `collectArmInfos`, `createSkeleton`, `armPanes` (`session.go:86`), the key computed from the saved id and baked into `--hook-key`, so firing is correct independent of the re-stamp, which precedes the helper launch and serves only the post-restore concerns. The firing path must not be changed to read the live id.
why: Reading the live id would make firing depend on re-stamp ordering and reintroduce a rename-window race.

text: No rename interception anywhere: Portal's in-TUI rename (`renameAndRefresh`, `internal/tui/model.go`) keeps doing a bare `RenameSession` and list refresh with no hook re-keying, and an external `tmux rename-session` is covered because it leaves `@portal-id` untouched.
why: With the name out of the key nothing has to observe a rename, the decisive advantage over intercept-and-rekey, which could only fix the in-TUI path.

text: The out-of-repo start-hook keeps calling `portal hooks set --on-resume` exactly as today, Portal resolving the stable key internally; nothing outside this repository changes.
why: Registration resolves the key inside Portal, so its callers need no change.

text: The `@portal-skeleton-*` markers (`internal/state/markers.go`, keyed by `SanitizePaneKey(name, w, p)`) are not re-anchored to `@portal-id`: they are transient, living only in the restore-to-hydration window, cleared on hydration and reaped by bootstrap steps 9–10, so a rename in that window at most strands a marker that is then cleaned.
why: Verified not affected the way hooks are: no persisted user data is lost, unlike hooks addressed across a reboot.

text: sessions.json delta and merge matching (`mergeSkippedPanes`, keyed by `SanitizePaneKey`) is not re-anchored: it governs only skeleton-marked panes during the restore window while capture is suppressed by `@portal-restoring`, and after restore a rename re-captures the session under its new name, which is correct.
why: Verified not affected: no silent loss.

text: The `@portal-active-*` marker the investigation listed as potentially affected does not exist in the code, only in a stale test comment, so no action is needed.
how: Read from the code.

text: Unit tests for the derivation primitives: `tmux.HookKey` returns `<id>:w.p` with an id and `<name>:w.p` without, covering distinct `w.p` suffixes under one id; `HookKeyFormat` resolves correctly against a real tmux session stamped and un-stamped; and for a stamped session the registration read, the cleanup enumeration and the restore baker produce byte-identical keys.
why: Correctness rests on every key-producing site deriving the same key.

text: Component tests: `CreateFromDir` and `QuickStart` stamp `@portal-id` and a stamp failure doesn't fail creation; capture reads the id into `Session.PortalID`, `""` when un-stamped; a sessions.json without `portal_id` decodes to `""` with no error or version bump; restore re-stamps from the saved value and skips the stamp when it is empty.
why: Covers stamping and the persistence chain at component level.

text: Integration tests for the rename gap: register a hook, rename, restore and assert the hook fires rather than bare `$SHELL`, for both raw `tmux rename-session` and `renameAndRefresh`; after a rename and restore, simulate the next capture and a second restore and assert the id is re-persisted and the hook fires again; run restore then the stale cleanup and assert the restored hook entry is not deleted.
why: Rename-then-restore had zero coverage, and durability across repeated reboots depends on the persistence chain.

text: Integration tests for legacy sessions: a pre-fix name-keyed hooks.json entry for an un-stamped, never-renamed session still resolves and is not mass-orphaned by stale cleanup after upgrade, and an un-stamped session degrades gracefully throughout, with no panic and the name-based key everywhere.
why: Guards the no-migration upgrade.

text: An integration test that per-pane hooks under one session stay independently addressable and fire for the correct pane after a rename and restore.
why: Guards against a multi-pane regression under the new key.

text: The fix's tests use no `t.Parallel()`; daemon-spawning and bootstrap-subprocess tests use `portaltest.IsolateStateForTest` and apply its env; real-tmux scenarios use the `tmuxtest` socket fixtures, restore scaffolding `restoretest`, and integration tests build the binary through the `portalbintest` / `restoretest` helpers.
why: Package-level mock injection rules out parallel tests, and the isolation helpers keep tests off the real system.

text: The primary risk is a missed key-producing site: any current or future caller building a hook key or live-key set from the name-based `StructuralKeyFormat` orphans stamped sessions' hooks at scale, the original symptom. Mitigated by one shared `HookKeyFormat` / `HookKey` primitive at every site and the cross-site consistency test.
how: Read from the code's key derivation sites, as the spec's risks assess them.

text: Accept best-effort stamping's risk: a swallowed stamp failure leaves that session on the name fallback, rename-vulnerable like a legacy session, non-fatal and self-correcting on its next recreation.
why: Stamping must never fail session creation, and the fallback degrades only to today's behaviour.

text: Fix complexity is medium, touching hook-key derivation at registration, capture and restore, and cleanup, plus creation stamping; regression risk is medium, since the hook-key format is shared across releases and subsystems and a careless change can orphan every existing hook at scale, while the stable-id approach is low-risk to the rename case itself.
how: Read from the code, as the investigation's risk assessment judges it.

text: Ship the fix in a regular release, not a hotfix.
why: It is an architectural keying change, with an additive schema field and changes across registration, capture, restore and cleanup, not a one-liner.

cites.section: What "skip" means — classifying the 11 steps > Context

text: Reject the all-or-nothing skip: two named paths, selected by the latch. Full bootstrap (latch not satisfied) runs the orchestrator and then sets the latch; abridged bootstrap (latch satisfied) runs the EnsureSaver liveness probe only and skips everything else.
why: The steps are not the same kind of work: some are once-per-lifetime and pointless on a latched server, one is an ongoing safety net that must keep running.
rules_out: Skipping all steps whenever the latch is set

text: The steps fall into three classes. Class 1, cold-only (EnsureServer, RegisterPortalHooks, SetRestoring, SweepOrphanDaemons, Restore, EagerSignalHydrate, ClearRestoring): skipped when latched. Class 2, protective liveness (EnsureSaver): kept on every abridged command. Class 3, cleanup (CleanStaleMarkers, SweepOrphanFIFOs, CleanStale hooks): marker and FIFO sweeps stay in the full bootstrap, hooks CleanStale leaves the orchestrator.
why: Latched, the server is up (else the latch died with it); hooks converged once and nothing re-adds them mid-lifetime; restore is a cold-boot concern; the orphan-daemon sweep targets prior-lifetime leftovers, the daemon flock and self-supervision keeping N<=1 within a lifetime.

text: The two paths are named full bootstrap and abridged bootstrap, never cold and warm; the latch, not whether the server was running, is the switch. A hand-started tmux server hit by x has no latch and gets the full bootstrap.
why: Cold/warm collides with 'is the tmux server running'; the two usually coincide but are not identical.

text: Full and abridged are not different programs: the full path is the existing Orchestrator.Run, run concurrently behind the loading screen on the TUI path and synchronously otherwise; the loading screen is a slow-path wrapper, not a distinct bootstrap.
why: Grounding of how the bootstrap is invoked.

text: There is exactly one abridged path, run identically by every command against an already-bootstrapped server; variants such as an open flavour that cleans and an attach flavour that doesn't are rejected.
why: User directive. It is load-bearing: it forces hooks cleanup out of the orchestrator entirely.
rules_out: Multiple abridged variants classified by command

text: Does EnsureSaver stay on the latched path, so a daemon that dies mid-lifetime is still revived?

cites.section: Protective steps stay on the warm path (EnsureSaver) > Context

text: Keep EnsureSaver on every abridged command as a cheap probe plus a re-ensure when the saver is down (Option B), and separately pursue making the daemon as robust as possible as ongoing work not gated by this feature.
why: Weeks-long server lifetimes mean recovery can't lean on a restart, and a self-ejected daemon would otherwise stay dead for weeks, silently losing scrollback capture and resurrection state. The probe costs ~1 tmux call: a healthy saver means 20 cheap probes under the burst, a dead one a flock-serialised single re-create. The person: 'Our fail-safe is great to keep.'

A pure latch relying on a hardened daemon that never needs external revival
alternatives: A: pure latch; saver revived only at server restart and by self-supervision
C: pure latch plus hardening the daemon so it never dies, judged unachievable in practice

text: Abridged EnsureSaver is liveness-only: SaverPanePIDOrAbsent, then BootstrapPortalSaver when absent. The version-gate (EnsurePortalSaverVersion's kill-and-recreate through the guarded kill-barrier) lives only in the full bootstrap, which a version bump triggers through a mismatched latch.

Cleanup is not run every 1s tick: it is throttled through a cheap per-tick time.Since(lastCleanup) >= interval check, the body firing only once the interval has elapsed. The interval defaults to 10s; its exact value is a tuning detail.

alternatives: Trigger cleanup only when the live-session set shrinks (noted, not chosen)

text: Cleanup sits on the tick's idle branch: after the @portal-restoring check, at the !dirty && !gap point, replacing the bare idle return with 'check the throttle, maybe clean, return'. text: lastCleanup is initialised to the daemon's start time, not the zero time, so the first cleanup fires one interval (~10s) after daemon start rather than on the first idle tick.
