What shape and chrome does the panel take?

The selector is a full-height, right-edge, non-blanking overlay with a left border only, rendered through the existing lipgloss v2 Compositor overlay mechanism, with the list behind it visible and re-theming live.

text: Panel surfaces use existing tokens only: body canvas; left border and header rule border; header label accent.mode; cursor row the shipped selection treatment; valid row label text.primary; slot badges accent.primary; invalid row label text.subtle; invalid ⚠ and reason, and the pinned dir row, accent.attention; footer keys accent.key with labels text.muted; confirm text.secondary; failed-commit ⚠ and text accent.attention with no band.
why: No 20th token; every surface resolving to an existing token keeps the colour-literal and swap-and-diff guards free of carve-outs; text.faint is decorative-only and the invalid label must be readable; ● marks assignment, not liveness.

text: The reference frames' panel chrome (#0C0C16 on a #2B3050 border) is not adopted.
why: Per-frame literals; expressing it would need a 20th token failing the promotion rule.

text: The panel does not animate: opening and closing are one frame each, 'slide-over' naming the shape, not a motion.
why: An animated open would fire OSC 11 repeatedly, render uncovered intermediate widths, and race t followed by Esc.

text: The panel has a vertical keymap footer (⏎ set theme / d set as dark / l set as light / esc close) and its cursor row uses the shipped selection treatment.
why: A horizontal keymap does not fit ~30 columns, and the vertical form matches the help modal; the cursor row reads as the same kind of list as Sessions.

text: The panel header is a one-row border rule then the label Themes, with no count; the rule sits in the page's rule lane so Themes lands on the page's section-header row, degrading to a compact two-row form below the height that affords alignment.
why: Matches the Sessions section-header idiom; the implementation review corrected label-then-rule to rule-then-label.

text: A single-row message slot above the footer, not reserved when empty, arbitrates two contenders (the slot-from-constant confirm and a failed commit); it may wrap at minimum width but is truncated to one line at minimum height.
why: The two contenders can never be live at once; the height floor counts exactly one message row.

text: Accepted: the panel covers the right-hand column (header hint, row meta, the footer's right end), and its edge cuts wherever it falls, mid-label included; the main screen is not re-laid-out while the panel is open.
why: The theme is carried by the left of the screen; not reflowing keeps the swap an O(1) restyle and the previewed surface still.

text: What do the panel's keys do, and when is anything written?

The panel follows the picker idiom: arrows move and re-theme live with nothing written; Ctrl+arrows page; Enter commits a constant and clears both slots; d commits the dark slot and l the light slot, each clearing the constant; Esc closes, discarding an uncommitted preview; the panel stays open on every commit.

text: Every row is exactly one line, its elements competing in priority order: the ⚠ glyph always, the right-aligned ● badge, the label truncated with … down to three visible characters, then the terse reason, the first dropped when a badge competes.

text: An unreadable themes directory gets a pinned ⚠ dir unreadable chrome row directly beneath the header, not a list row: it costs a viewport row (counted in the height floor when present), is not counted by theme: enumerated, fits the minimum width at 16 columns, and built-in and persisted-slug rows still render beneath it.
why: A list row would vanish on paging; the warning is what stands between the user and silently missing drop-ins.

text: Arrow keys skip invalid rows, reusing the group-header skip mechanism, which composes with paging.
why: Invalid rows are unselectable.

text: Markers use inline slot badges (treatment A): right-aligned ● dark / ● light on assigned rows, ● both when both slots name one slug, and a bare ● for a constant; the two states never coexist on screen. The assignment block under the header (treatment B) is rejected.
why: Badges stay attached to their rows and scale with the library; B duplicates names and pushes the list down; ● both is determined and no wider than ● light.
rules_out: Treatment B assignment header

text: ● is the right badge glyph: Portal already repurposes it for multi-select marking, so it is the general marked/active glyph; ● marks assignment and the ▌ plus tint cursor marks browse position.
why: Lee corrected the spike's reasoning that ● means attached only.

text: Accepted caveat: with a very long list the assignments could scroll out of view.
why: A user knows what they picked and can scroll to it.

text: A badge marks the slug a slot resolves to before fallback: the persisted slug when set (loadable or not, the fallback's row carrying none), the shipped default's slug when never set; both slots' badges always show, so Enter on a fresh install visibly collapses two badges to one bare ●.
why: ● means what is set, and the shipped-default rule gives it a home on a fresh install with no prefs.json.

text: Which key opens the panel, where, and what blocks or routes input?

cites.section: Opening the panel — `t`, on Sessions and Projects

cites.section: 9.6 Opening the panel — `t`, on Sessions and Projects

text: Only a modal, a pending burst, NO_COLOR, a terminal below the render floor and the unbound pages block t; below the floor t refuses with a flash per dimension.
why: The render floor is an entry condition as well as a resize condition.

why: Previewing mid-selection is legitimate since the marked-row ● is themed. Lee: I might want to see the theme while multi-selecting.

text: During a pending burst t is swallowed, consistent with the burst's input lock.
why: Lee: a pending burst shouldn't allow any key behaviour.

cites.section: Input routing while the panel is open (the review's F8)

text: The panel is key-exclusive: it owns arrows, Enter, d, l and Esc, swallows everything else, and keeps Ctrl-C live.
why: Pass-through would let k kill a session or x swap pages behind the panel; swallowing Ctrl-C would remove the exit key.

text: Blocked t flashes where the key is bound and could be expected to work (NO_COLOR on Sessions/Projects) and is silent where it is not bound (Preview, modals, burst-locked).
why: Exactly how s already behaves.

text: How does the panel handle narrow and short terminals?

The panel has a fixed preferred width of ~24 to 30 columns, shrinks toward a minimum as the terminal narrows, truncates long slugs with …, and refuses with a flash only when even the minimum cannot render.
why: A narrow terminal is a space shortage, where Portal's doctrine is degrade, never break; the multi-select block is a capability absence and does not transfer. Lee: like on a mobile, I would still expect it to open.

text: What are the panel's exact width and height degradation thresholds? They are pinned at implementation.

Height overflow scrolls through bubbles/list with Ctrl+arrow paging; the minimum height is header plus footer plus one row plus one message row (plus the dir row when present), below which t refuses with a flash.
why: Both message contenders are non-suppressible, so a floor without the message row would put the panel one row short when a message appears.

text: On resize the panel degrades in place and closes with a flash only below the render floor; a forced close takes the Esc path exactly and silently cancels a live confirm.
why: Any other behaviour would strand the user rendering a theme they never chose with no room to reopen the panel; nothing is written before a confirm resolves.

text: There is no panel key to unset a theme back to the shipped default; returning means setting tokyo-night explicitly, which converts an inherited default into a pin. Accepted and documented.
why: It only bites if the shipped default changes, and prefs.json is hand-editable.
rules_out: A clear/unset key

text: Under NO_COLOR t is blocked with a flash and its help row filtered out through the same call-site filter that drops m.
why: There is no colour to theme, a capability absence rather than a space shortage, so the panel would be inert.

text: Under NO_COLOR the theme machinery runs unchanged: both nominated themes load, the gate is skipped so dark selects the active member, theme: loaded is emitted, and the startup canvas hex is captured though no canvas is painted.
why: Not special-casing the loader keeps a commit's state in hand; the counter that blocking prevents setting a theme for other contexts is accepted because prefs.json is hand-editable.

text: The panel's own chrome re-themes with the previewed theme, no exceptions; the residue is that a legal-but-awful drop-in can render the panel unreadable, recoverable only by editing prefs.json if committed.
why: It is the honest preview, avoids a render-layer exception the swap guard would have to carve out, and Esc is a keypress not a visible affordance. Lee: yes everything rethemes.

cites.section: The panel re-themes too (the review's F2)

text: The panel's six keys (arrows, Ctrl+arrows, Enter, d, l, Esc) live in the keymap descriptor as a panel scope; its vertical footer renders the Core entries (Enter, d, l, Esc), arrows being non-core; keymap_dispatch_guard_test covers them; ? does nothing inside the panel.
why: A bespoke footer would be a second place labels go stale; there is no panel help modal to show.

text: What happens when a theme commit fails to write?
A failed write reports ⚠ in the message slot until the next keypress, keeps the theme applied in memory, and does not move the ●.
why: Applied but not persisted becomes a reported state; ● means what is persisted.

text: A failure is outstanding until a later commit succeeds; closing with one outstanding raises the main-screen flash 'theme not saved — see portal.log', which discharges it; on a forced close that flash wins over the geometry flash; Ctrl-C leaves the report to the log alone.
why: Esc re-resolves from persisted state, so without a surviving report the revert would be silent; there is no surface to flash into on Ctrl-C and stderr is reserved for bootstrap failures.

text: A commit is always re-attemptable by pressing the commit key again, with no special retry affordance.
why: Commit keys are unconditional writes.

text: The picker half of the panel has strong prior art (Helix :theme, Ghostty +list-themes, kitty's themes kitten), but assigning a theme to a light/dark slot from inside a picker was found in no surveyed tool; Helix, Ghostty, Zellij, kitty and bat all require editing config for the pair.

text: Is live re-theming achievable and cheap, and what makes it complete?

why: The panel is a third bubbles/list instance whose theme changes on every arrow.

why: The race it exists for is the startup query reply against Portal's own canvas set.

text: The startup canvas hex is captured and retained as model state and RestoreTerminalBackground's comparison anchors to it; canvasHexFor becomes theme-agnostic; a direct unit test drives RestoreTerminalBackground without fixtures across a mid-session commit and a Ctrl-C quit with an uncommitted preview.

text: How are theme outcomes logged?
A new theme log component is added to the closed taxonomy by spec amendment, with attr keys slug, slot, reason, path, token, count and rejected.
why: Unlike the dumb prefs and terminals stores, the loader has parse, validate and fallback outcomes, and a TUI launch that rejects a theme should leave a passive record. Lee: logging is good because it helps diagnose problems.

text: Event catalogue: theme: loaded (INFO, one line per nomination at construction, at the off-construction commit load, and for the fallback when a nomination fails); theme: enumerated (INFO, every panel open, count of rows and rejected unselectable rows); theme: rejected (WARN, per file, deduped per process on slug+reason or path+reason); theme: directory unusable (WARN, deduped on path+reason); theme: fallback applied (WARN, deduped on slug+reason); theme: appearance migrated (INFO, on successful persist); theme: commit failed (WARN, per failed write).
why: Each line carries the attrs that make it greppable; dedup keeps a passive trail from becoming running commentary across panel opens.

text: Emission is controlled by an injected logger: a real component logger on TUI construction, the panel and the persister, and log.Discard on doctor, theme export and capturetool; the per-process dedup state lives on that injected logger.
why: The component records where a theme is used, never where it is diagnosed: doctor and export are the user looking, and emitting from doctor would put the largest WARN volume where it is least needed.

text: Rejections log at WARN, not INFO.
why: Doctor treats them as advisory for exit-code purposes, but 'your config did not work' is a warning in a log.

text: How are bundled themes contrast-checked?

cites.section: Verification — four resolutions (the review's F4, F5, F14, F15)

text: Floor checks auto-enumerate the embedded set, so a new built-in is checked by default, and every ratio is measured against the theme's own canvas, never a constant.
why: Enrolment must be automatic for the bundled tier to mean anything.

text: The canonical rule set, with floors 4.50 normal, 3.00 UI and 1.10 fill: text.primary to text.muted at 4.50 or above; text.subtle in 3.00 to 4.49; text.faint above 1.00 and below 3.00; accent.primary 3.00 or above; accent.key, accent.mode, accent.attention and both states 4.50 or above; border and canvas unfloored; bg.selection and bg.attention each with text-on-tint 4.50, bar against canvas 3.00 and fill 1.10; bg.subtle fill 1.10 only; text.on-selection, text.secondary, text.tertiary and state.positive on bg.selection and text.on-attention on bg.attention at 4.50; state.positive must clear both canvas and bg.selection.
why: Auto-enumeration only means anything against a complete, theme-independent list; the Nord table is one walk of it.

text: Light themes carry additional exact-value pins on four eyeball-pinned tints (bg.selection, bg.attention, bg.subtle, border) with nothing relaxed; a test-side light/dark table enrols themes for TestLightSurfaceTintsPinned and TestLightTintFillsArePerceptible and asserts every embedded theme appears in it.
why: Light-tint-on-light-canvas is numerically insufficient, so the pin is the only guard; a forgotten entry must fail the suite; the count of four decides which pin notes move into theme files.

text: docs/theming.md gets a guard that parses its token table and compares the name set with Theme.All(), and its example theme must parse and contain all 19 keys; the discovery half has no automated check.
why: The doc is now the sole record of the ramp and role meanings, and the stale '2-tone border' claim was found by chance.

text: Which existing tests change and which new tests are added?

TestMVTokenCount moves to 19 meaning 'the vocabulary is 19'; TestMVDarkVariantsPinned, TestEachTokenCarriesLightVariant and TestEveryTokenHasLightVariant are deleted; TestLightSurfaceTintsPinned and TestLightTintFillsArePerceptible survive and become per-light-theme; the ten floor tests in contrast_test.go are rewritten with a loop over embedded themes (TestContrastMath untouched).
why: Exact-hex pins duplicate the data files; the ColorFor tests cannot compile; the floor tests rest on theme.MV, .Dark/.Light, mode subtests and the hardcoded canvases, all removed.

text: New tests: a table-driven loader/parser test over the lexical branches, hex domain, slug charset, reserved check and the reason ladder; a prefs and migration test covering the mapping, trigger versus no-op, marker rules, raw appearance round-trip, RMW merge and file creation; a panel behaviour test through the ThemeEnumerator seam; a nomination resolution and fallback test; plus the embedded-set validity test, the swap guard, the restore anchor test and the doc guard.
why: The loader is the most branch-heavy component; the prefs path's failure silently destroys a user's config; the panel's deterministic rules have no other home.

text: keymap_dispatch_guard_test extends to the panel scope; the colour-literal guard keeps its mechanism and scope over internal/tui but its theme-subpackage exemption is deleted.
why: The theme package moves out of internal/tui and holds no hex values, which live in the .theme files.

text: The colour-literal guard flags only a basic-literal argument to lipgloss.Color within internal/tui: it does not see lipgloss.ANSIColor, struct-literal colour types, dependency-default colours or anything in internal/capture.
how: Read from colour_literal_guard_test.go during the background review.

cites.section: B1. Corrections to claims made during this session

text: Should Portal offer transparent themes that use the terminal's own background?

Transparent themes are deferred, not rejected, until there are enough themes for the question to be real; the file format leaves the door open and following the terminal background keeps adding them purely additive.
why: With a library, a theme that clashes can be swapped for another; deferring is cheap because a transparent theme needs no new detection mechanism.

text: Transparency is feasible: NO_COLOR already suppresses all three canvas sites, but one colourless boolean drops both hue and canvas, so it would need splitting into independent no-hue and no-canvas flags; if shipped, validation becomes bimodal (floors cannot be evaluated without a canvas) and the panel must opt back into a background.
how: Read from header.go's colourless branch and the canvas sites during research.

text: The panel has no search or filtering of the theme list for now.
why: Themes will be added over time, not in bulk, and famous palettes skew dark, so interleaving pressure arrives late; kitty and Ghostty add fuzzy search when libraries grow.

text: Ecosystem detection: bat, delta, Neovim and yazi detect light/dark by default; where opt-in, the shape is naming two themes (Helix's Constant or Adaptive{light, dark, fallback}, Zellij's theme_dark and theme_light); dark is the universal no-answer fallback; emulators (Ghostty, kitty, iTerm2) track the OS appearance, not the terminal's colours.
how: From the ecosystem deep dive's documentation and source survey.

text: A theme is overwhelmingly one palette with siblings as separate themes, paired by naming convention, two settings, an inline mapping, in-palette metadata (tinted8 requires variant) or derivation from the background; real families are not 1:1 (Catppuccin one light and three darks, Dracula and Nord dark-only, Zellij's 41 built-ins holding six sibling pairs).
how: From the ecosystem deep dive.

cites.section: A3. Pairing: five distinct ways the ecosystem expresses light↔dark

text: No terminal application surveyed prompts on first run; the one counter-example in the wider ecosystem, Powerlevel10k's wizard, relies on an interactive shell already drawing a prompt.
how: From the ecosystem deep dive.

text: Several tools sidestep light/dark by inheriting the terminal's ANSI palette (lazygit, gitui, fzf, Helix's base16_default); btop alone offers a hex theme plus an opt-out of owning the background. Portal's canvas ownership is the deliberate opposite choice.
how: From the ecosystem deep dive.

cites.section: A5. A fourth strategy Portal has already rejected by owning a canvas

text: There is no format consensus: each tool uses its own config format, and Ghostty and kitty treat a theme as a config file; partial merge over a base is the modern direction (gitui, atuin, Helix, yazi); themes live in a library directory with selection as one config line, and GUI-adjacent pickers write a machine-owned file.
how: From the ecosystem deep dive.

text: Token vocabularies run from 8 to about 105 keys, and use-site naming is the norm (Helix names its UI half by use-site); Charm's Crush encodes intrinsic prominence in comparative ladders and documents onPrimary as a contrast pairing.
how: From the ecosystem deep dive.

cites.section: A8. Prior art for weight-based naming (directly relevant to the border rename)

text: No surveyed terminal application validates user colours for contrast; Ghostty's minimum-contrast is an off-by-default draw-time clamp that destroys hue where it engages, and neither base16 nor tinted8 imposes contrast requirements; Portal's numerically verified floors appear more rigorous than anything surveyed.
how: From the ecosystem deep dive.
